auditFocus: raw `new`/`delete` or manual `malloc`/`free` where RAII/a smart pointer (`unique_ptr`/`shared_ptr`) already fits the ownership model
a pointer or reference returned to, or captured from, a local/stack-destroyed object (use-after-free / dangling reference)
a container iterator or pointer used after the container it points into was resized, erased from, or reallocated
an unchecked `malloc`/`new` return, or a missing `free`/destructor on an error/early-return path in C
signed integer overflow, unvalidated array/index bounds, or an out-of-bounds access on a fixed-size buffer
a shared variable read/written from more than one thread with no mutex/atomic guarding it
a memory-safety or UB bug report whose verification step never mentions AddressSanitizer/UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer/ThreadSanitizer
buildCommands: cmake -S . -B build-asan -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS='-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer -g' && cmake --build build-asan && ctest --test-dir build-asan
fixGuardrails: never silence a sanitizer finding by disabling the sanitizer, adding a suppression, or narrowing what it scans instead of fixing the underlying memory/UB bug
never replace a real bounds/null check with a cast or a suppression comment to make a warning disappear
never widen an unsafe C API (`strcpy`, `sprintf`, `gets`) back in while resolving an unrelated failure
fix the smallest root cause; do not refactor unrelated ownership or threading code while resolving a single build/test/sanitizer failure
